name: Koparion
isnote: Chure 1994 assigned the tooth to Troodontidae; Wikipedia revision 1362754182 calls it only a small coelurosaurian theropod, and Hunt & Lucas 2006 discuss a small theropod from the Upper Jurassic of New Mexico in the same context. No analysis places it more precisely.
sum: Small theropod known from a single tooth from the Kimmeridgian Morrison Formation of Utah, first read as the oldest troodontid.
wsnote: The tooth crown is 2 mm tall (Wikipedia revision 1362754182); no body size can be given.
holotype: DINO 3353, a single maxillary tooth crown (root missing), Brushy Basin Member, Morrison Formation, Rainbow Park, Uintah County, Utah.
biology: The tooth is tiny, strongly recurved, and serrated on both edges with low rectangular denticles; nothing about its way of life is stated in the sources.
author: Chure 1994

sources.text: Adrian P. Hunt, Spencer G. Lucas 2006. A SMALL THEROPOD DINOSAUR FROM THE UPPER JURASSIC OF EASTERN NEW MEXICO WITH A CHECKLIST OF SMALL THEROPODS FROM THE MORRISON FORMATION OF WESTERN NORTH AMERICA. .

dates_note: No PBDB record. Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation, late Kimmeridgian, about 151 Ma (Wikipedia revision 1362754182); ICS bounds of the stage used.
